Recurring Journal Entry

Create journal entries that repeat on a regular schedule.

Useful for monthly accruals, depreciation, or other regular adjustments.

Next issue date

The date when the next journal entry will be automatically created. This date advances automatically based on your frequency settings.

For month-end adjustments, set this to the last day of the month. The system checks daily for entries due to be created.

Interval

The frequency interval for creating journal entries. This number works with the period type to set your adjustment schedule.

Common examples: 1 Month = monthly adjustments, 3 Months = quarterly entries, 1 Year = annual adjustments.

PeriodType

The period type that works with the interval to determine frequency. Select the unit of time for your accounting cycle.

Most accounting adjustments are monthly. Use 'Days' for daily accruals or 'Years' for annual adjustments.

MonthDay

For monthly recurring entries, specify which day of the month the journal entry should be created.

'Last day of month' is common for month-end adjustments. Choose specific days for mid-month allocations.

ExpirationType

Determines when the recurring schedule ends. This controls how long the system will continue creating journal entries.

Choose 'Until further notice' for perpetual adjustments like depreciation, or 'Until date' for temporary accruals.

UntilDate

The date when recurring journal entries will stop being created. The system will not create any entries after this date.

Use this for prepaid expenses that will be fully amortized or accruals that will reverse by a specific date.

Currency

The currency for this journal entry template. Leave blank to use the base currency.

Only specify a foreign currency if you need to record adjustments in a currency other than your base currency.

Narration

A description or explanation for the journal entry that will be copied to each generated entry.

Be descriptive to help with audit trails. Examples: 'Monthly depreciation - Equipment', 'Quarterly insurance expense allocation', 'Monthly payroll accrual'.

Lines

The debit and credit lines that make up the journal entry. Total debits must equal total credits for the entry to be valid.

Each line represents either a debit or credit to a specific account. Add multiple lines as needed for complex adjustments.

The same amounts will be used for each generated entry unless you edit this template.

Specify the tax transaction type when tax codes are used in the journal entry lines.

This determines how the transaction affects your tax reports. Only required if you're using tax codes in the entry.

Automatic reference

When enabled, the system automatically assigns sequential reference numbers to each generated journal entry.

Recommended for audit trail purposes. The system will ensure each entry has a unique identifier.
